newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-REYNOLDS INSISTS HE'S NOT DONE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-REYNOLDS INSISTS HE'S NOT DONE.

text.p: As the runners raced toward the finish line, world 400-meter record holder Butch Reynolds fell farther and farther behind, finally finishing sixth.
Reynolds's plan for the U.S. championships -- to run 42 or 43 seconds in the absence of injured Olympic and world champion Michael Johnson -- had failed miserably.

"I gambled today, but I'm not done," said the 33-year-old two-time world silver medalist. "I'm looking forward to more racing. I was going for sub-43 seconds and got out really hard (20.7 for 200 meters). I was ready spiritually and mentally, but not physically. Now I have to go back and work on that part.
"Everybody's talking about breaking the world record (43.29 seconds). It's my world record and I'm going to break it this year."
